_test_notes.purpose: Comprehensive-depth test run of funding-scan-prompt.md (v2: depth-of-coverage, Closed - Recurring, not_eligible) against Cardinal Construction, LLC. Four parallel sub-scans (Maryland state / federal / local+Delaware / private+corporate+industry) merged and deduplicated. Profile built from public sources; fields marked ASSUMED were not publicly stated.
_test_notes.method: ~115 web searches and ~190 page fetches across four research agents; every item below was read on the cited page unless marked Needs Verification.

profile.industry: Construction — commercial general contracting, concrete, demolition, site prep, residential remodeling, structural steel/precast
profile.service_area: Maryland Eastern Shore (Talbot, Dorchester, Caroline, Kent, Queen Anne's); Delaware (Kent, Sussex)
profile.licenses_enrollments: MDOT-certified MBE/DBE/SBE; Delaware Office of Supplier Diversity certified; licensed, insured and bonded in MD and DE
profile.services: Commercial general contracting, construction management, commercial concrete, demolition, site prep, residential remodeling
profile.expansion_interests: Partnering with larger primes on multimillion-dollar commercial projects; growing bonding capacity; equipment purchases (ASSUMED from owner interview)

key_context_findings: DECADE Act of 2026 (HB0898, eff. 7/1/2026) raised MSBDFA caps (contract financing/guaranty $2M→$3M; surety guaranty $2.25M→$3M; direct bonds $2.5M→$5M) and repealed the restriction limiting contract financing/bonding to government and utility contracts. Commerce's page confirms the amendment but publishes no figures; MMG's page still shows pre-DECADE figures. [VERIFY operating limits with MMG.]
SBA final rule 91 FR 51568 (eff. 9/10/2026) removed the race-based presumption of social disadvantage for 8(a); Black ownership alone no longer establishes eligibility.
USDOT final rule (9/25/2026) has DelDOT re-evaluating all DBE firms; DBE contract goals in Delaware are paused.
Easton is a Maryland Enterprise Zone and a DHCD Sustainable Community; [VERIFY] Cardinal's address falls inside the boundaries.
WOTC lapsed for wages after 12/31/2025; MBDA center operations remain subject to pending litigation.

items.fit: Right-sized county job in Cardinal's own county. Prior county bids required 5% bid security and 100% performance and payment bonds.
items.verify_notes: [VERIFY] County bid pages returned fetch errors; details from an aggregator. Call County Manager's Office / Finance (410-770-8020) for the package.

items.name: MSBDFA Surety Bond Program
items.funder: Maryland Department of Commerce (administered by Meridian Management Group)
items.award_amount: Guaranty up to 90% of surety loss. Statutory caps post-DECADE Act (eff. 7/1/2026): guaranty up to $3M, direct bid/performance/payment bonds up to $5M. MMG's page still shows prior $2.5M caps. [VERIFY]
items.synopsis: Bid, payment and performance bond guaranties to sureties, and in some cases direct bonds, for Maryland small businesses — with explicit focus on socially and economically disadvantaged owners — that cannot obtain bonding on reasonable terms. The 2026 DECADE Act removed the former limitation to government/utility-funded contracts and raised caps effective July 1, 2026. Commerce's page notes online applications are not currently available; apply through MMG.

eligibility.notes: Maryland principal place of business; 100% Black-owned (exceeds the 70% disadvantaged-ownership rule); must show inability to obtain adequate bonding through normal channels.

items.fit: The single most on-point program for the bonding-capacity goal, and the 2026 expansion to private contracts makes it relevant to Cardinal's commercial work, not only public jobs.
items.compliance_flag: ⚠ Statute amended effective 7/1/2026; confirm current operating limits, fees and whether private commercial contracts are now accepted before relying on figures. Contractors must register for state EFT before any BPW-approved contract over $200,000.
items.verify_notes: Statutory limits from HB0898 fiscal note (https://mgaleg.maryland.gov/2026RS/fnotes/bil_0008/hb0898.pdf). MMG: https://mmgcapitalgroup.com/msbdfa/, 410-333-4270.

items.name: MSBDFA Contract Financing Program
items.funder: Maryland Department of Commerce (Meridian Management Group)
items.award_amount: Up to $3M post-DECADE (was $2M); generally Prime + 2%; term tied to contract. [VERIFY]
items.synopsis: Direct loans or guaranties for working capital and equipment needed to perform an awarded contract. Historically limited to government or regulated-utility contracts; that limitation was repealed effective July 1, 2026. Requires assignment of contract proceeds and, per MMG, a bank turndown letter.

eligibility.notes: Same criteria as the surety program; must hold or be awarded a contract to finance.

items.fit: Lets Cardinal mobilize on larger awards without straining cash flow; equipment purchase under a contract is an allowed use.
items.compliance_flag: ⚠ Confirm post-DECADE contract eligibility rules with MMG.

items.name: MSBDFA Long-Term Guaranty Program
items.funder: Maryland Department of Commerce (Meridian Management Group)
items.award_amount: Guaranty of the lesser of 80% of loan or $2M (MMG page); statutory cap $3M post-DECADE. [VERIFY]
items.synopsis: Guarantees bank loans to eligible businesses for working capital, equipment, real estate and leasehold improvements, and may provide an interest subsidy. 2025 legislation lets MSBDFA back guaranties with letters of credit or escrow.

eligibility.notes: Same disadvantaged-owner, Maryland small-business criteria.

items.fit: Useful for an equipment term loan through a local bank when collateral or track record is thin.

items.name: Maryland Economic Adjustment Fund (MEAF)
items.funder: Maryland Department of Commerce, Office of Finance Programs
items.award_amount: Up to $150,000; rate and term not stated [VERIFY]
items.synopsis: Direct loans for small and underserved businesses with fewer than 50 employees — skilled trades named — for working capital, equipment, building renovation, real estate and site improvements. Applicants must show creditworthiness and inability to qualify for traditional lending. Page states new applications are being accepted.

eligibility.notes: Fewer than 50 employees; skilled trades explicitly included; statewide.

items.fit: Right-sized for an equipment purchase at Cardinal's scale and faster than SSBCI products that start at $250K.
items.verify_notes: Requires business plan with 3-year projections, personal financial statement, two years of tax returns. Contact on page: 410-767-6356, meafloanfund@maryland.gov.

items.name: DHCD Small Business Companion Loans (SSBCI)
items.funder: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
items.award_amount: $250,000–$5,000,000; 4% fixed; up to 30 years; ≤50% of project cost; 1:1 private match required
items.synopsis: DHCD lends alongside a private lender (DHCD will help identify one) for property, equipment, working capital and tenant improvements. Owner-occupancy rules apply to real estate; residential construction is excluded as a use. Personal guarantees from owners over 20%.

eligibility.notes: Fewer than 500 employees; commercial use; not on excluded-business list.

items.fit: Good for an equipment package or shop/yard purchase if Cardinal can attract a bank partner for the matching half. The $250K minimum may exceed current need.

items.name: DHCD Own Your Future (SSBCI) — owner-occupied commercial real estate
items.funder: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
items.award_amount: $250,000–$5,000,000; 4% fixed; up to 30 years; ≤50% of project; 1:1 private match
items.synopsis: Finances purchase, construction, expansion or renovation of commercial property the business will occupy (51% for acquisition/renovation; 60% for new construction). Projects of $500K or less may qualify for a $250K matched loan without the occupancy test.

eligibility.notes: Only relevant if Cardinal intends to buy a shop or yard.

items.fit: Relevant only if a facility purchase is in the growth plan.

items.name: DHCD Small Business Direct Loans — competitive rounds
items.funder: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
items.last_round: Opened 2026-08-17, closed 2026-09-17; next round: not posted (press release says rounds announced quarterly)
items.award_amount: Up to $2,000,000 per loan at 4% fixed, up to 30 years; $14M in round 1
items.synopsis: Competitively scored direct loans (community impact, financial need, viability, readiness) for real estate, equipment, working capital and start-up/acquisition costs. Applicant must be in a Sustainable Community or Priority Funding Area. Preference to housing creation, child care, healthy food and vacant-property rehab.

eligibility.notes: Easton is a DHCD Sustainable Community; [VERIFY] Cardinal's address is inside the boundary. For-profit entities eligible.

items.fit: Moderate — scoring favors community-facing projects, but a Black-owned contractor rehabilitating a vacant Easton commercial property for its own shop could score well.
items.verify_notes: Sign up for round notifications on the program page and request a Business Development Officer consultation first.

items.name: Small, Minority & Women-Owned Businesses Account (VLT Fund) loans
items.funder: Maryland Department of Commerce via fund managers (closest: Maryland Capital Enterprises, Salisbury)
items.award_amount: Not stated; [VERIFY] with fund manager
items.synopsis: Casino (VLT) proceeds fund loans to small, minority and women-owned businesses through designated fund managers. Half targets areas around the six casinos; the rest is statewide. The DECADE Act shifts $5M/year of VLT revenue to MSBDFA beginning FY2027, which may reduce manager allocations.

eligibility.notes: Talbot County is not a casino target area, so Cardinal competes in the statewide pool. [VERIFY] which manager covers Talbot.

items.fit: Good secondary source for working capital or equipment at smaller scale.
items.verify_notes: Maryland Capital Enterprises, 410-546-1900.

items.name: Maryland Small Business Reserve (SBR) self-certification and Small Business Preference
items.funder: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
items.award_amount: Not stated — roughly 20% of open state-funded eMMA solicitations are SBR-designated; up to 5% price preference for certified small businesses
items.synopsis: Free self-certification through eMMA. Construction firms qualify with 50 or fewer employees and $7M or less average gross sales over three years. SBR solicitations are competed only among certified small businesses; certifications issued after 8/29/2025 are valid three years.

eligibility.notes: Cardinal is far under both thresholds. [VERIFY] whether its eMMA SBR flag is already active.

items.fit: Essential, zero-cost prerequisite for state prime work; stacks with existing MDOT MBE certification for the state's 29% MBE goal.

items.name: Maryland DGS construction procurement channel (eMMA)
items.funder: Maryland Department of General Services, Office of Design, Construction & Energy
items.award_amount: Varies per solicitation; all construction over $15,000 is posted on eMMA
items.synopsis: DGS posts all state facility construction bids and design-build RFPs on eMMA; many small renovation and IQC solicitations carry SBR designation. DGS MBE participation was 21.4% in FY2024 against a 29% goal, so primes actively seek certified MBE subcontractors.

eligibility.notes: SBR plus MBE certification.

items.fit: Primary state contract channel for a commercial GC; Eastern Shore state facilities (Chesapeake College, DNR, MDOT SHA District 2) are within reach.
items.verify_notes: eMMA search is login/robots-gated — see manual_checks.

items.name: MDOT SBE certification (automatic with DBE)
items.funder: MDOT Office of Minority Business Enterprise
items.award_amount: Not stated — SBE-only prime contracts on federally aided SHA/MTA/MAA projects
items.synopsis: Race- and gender-neutral program giving small firms prime-contract opportunities on federally funded transportation projects without competing against large firms. All MDOT DBE-certified firms are automatically SBE; no fee; annual affidavit.

eligibility.notes: Already DBE/SBE per profile; confirm listing in the MDOT online directory.

items.fit: Confirms a channel for small federal-aid highway and airport prime work.

items.name: MDOT SHA DBE Business Development Reimbursement Program (BDRP)
items.funder: MDOT State Highway Administration, Office of Equal Opportunity (federal DBE supportive services)

items.synopsis: Reimburses Maryland-headquartered MDOT-certified DBEs doing heavy-transportation work for training, estimating and bid software, audits, capability statements, memberships and one-on-one consulting including bonding and insurance. eligibility.notes: Eligible as MDOT DBE if NAICS codes cover transportation-related work (concrete, demolition, site prep qualify in principle).

items.fit: Small but directly funds bonding consulting, a financial review (which sureties require) and bid software.
items.verify_notes: [VERIFY] FFY26 reactivation with SHA OEO.

items.name: Maryland Apprenticeship Incentive Program (MAIP)
items.funder: Maryland Department of Labor, Office of Apprenticeship
items.award_amount: Up to $3,000 per adult registered apprentice; up to $7,500 per high-school-age apprentice
items.synopsis: Reimburses registered apprenticeship sponsors and employers for instruction, recruitment and supportive services for first-year apprentices who remain employed and registered at least seven months. Application due within 30 days of the apprentice's registration. $5M program under the RAISE Act of 2025.

eligibility.notes: Requires Cardinal to be a Registered Apprenticeship sponsor or signatory employer.

items.fit: Strong for building a crew in a tight Eastern Shore labor market; stacks with the apprenticeship tax credit.
items.verify_notes: [VERIFY] FY2027 funding availability; 410-767-2246.

items.name: Maryland Apprenticeship Tax Credit
items.award_amount: $3,000 per registered apprentice (first five), $1,000 each beyond; $1,000 per youth apprentice; $15,000 max per taxpayer per year
items.synopsis: Income tax credit for Maryland employers that sponsor or participate in a registered apprenticeship; apprentice must be in first year and employed at least seven months in the tax year.

eligibility.notes: Eligible once Cardinal participates in a registered apprenticeship.

items.fit: Modest but easy once apprenticeship participation is in place.
items.compliance_flag: ⚠ Maryland requires contractors on certain public-work contracts to participate in a registered apprenticeship or pay into the State Apprenticeship and Training Fund — a compliance item once Cardinal pursues state public work.
items.verify_notes: [VERIFY] current-year sunset/extension status.

items.name: Enterprise Zone Tax Credits — Easton Enterprise Zone
items.funder: Maryland Department of Commerce / Easton Economic Development Corporation (local administrator)
items.award_amount: Real property credit 80% of eligible assessment years 1–5 stepping to 30% by year 10; income tax credit $1,000 per qualified new employee, or $3,000/$2,000/$1,000 over 3 years for economically disadvantaged hires
items.synopsis: Businesses located within the Easton Enterprise Zone (downtown, Port St., Easton Point, Talbot Commerce Park, Mistletoe Hall park) that make capital improvements or hire new full-time employees can claim state income tax credits and local real property tax credits after local certification. eligibility.notes: Depends on whether Cardinal's business location is inside the zone boundary.

items.fit: Low-cost benefit if Cardinal hires or improves property in the zone; the disadvantaged-employee credit aligns with apprenticeship hiring.
items.verify_notes: Zone list: https://commerce.maryland.gov/Documents/BusinessResource/maryland.enterprise.zone.administrators.pdf. Contact Easton EDC for boundary map.

items.last_round: Closed to new applications; all current-fiscal-year funding obligated; historically reopens July 1 — next round: not posted

items.synopsis: Reimburses private employers with 500 or fewer employees for half the cost of training leading to industry-recognized credentials (OSHA 30, crane/rigging, estimating, project management).

eligibility.notes: Eligible when open.

items.fit: Good for credentialing crew and office staff to qualify for larger contracts.
items.verify_notes: [VERIFY] FY27 reopening date.

items.name: Job Creation Tax Credit (JCTC)
items.award_amount: $3,000 per net new job; $5,000 in a revitalization area (Easton qualifies); $1M per business per year max; $4M annual program cap
items.synopsis: Credit for creating full-time net new Maryland jobs paying at least 120% of state minimum wage within 24 months. Talbot is on the reduced-threshold county list, so the minimum is 10 new jobs rather than 60. Notify Commerce before hiring.

eligibility.notes: A 1–10 employee firm would need to add 10 FTEs; [VERIFY] whether construction is an eligible activity and whether the program's authorization is current (page shows a stale 2022 sunset alongside 2025 wage tables).

items.fit: Future-state only.

items.name: MEA FY27 Commercial & Community Buildings Grant Program (contractor channel)
items.award_amount: Program budget $103.9M (Track 1 Commercial Buildings $48.0M); per-project amounts in FOA [VERIFY]
items.synopsis: Competitive grants to commercial building owners, local governments and school systems for efficiency, electrification, renewable and storage projects. Applications via My MEA Portal; office hours 10/29, 11/12 and 12/3/2026; deadline December 9, 2026 at 3:00 PM ET.

eligibility.notes: Eligible only as a building owner for its own facility. Listed as a business-development channel: funded owners will need GCs for envelope, HVAC and electrical retrofits.

items.fit: Indirect — market Cardinal to Eastern Shore building owners and local governments applying under Tracks 1–2.
items.verify_notes: [VERIFY] whether installers need any registration to perform grant-funded work.

items.name: SBA Surety Bond Guarantee Program
items.funder: U.S. Small Business Administration, Office of Surety Guarantees
items.award_amount: Guarantees bonds on contracts up to $9M (non-federal) and $14M (federal with contracting officer certification). SBA reimburses the surety 90% of loss on contracts ≤$100K and on any contract for firms owned by socially and economically disadvantaged individuals; 80% otherwise (13 CFR 115.31). Contractor fee 0.6% of contract price on performance/payment bonds; no bid-bond fee. Quick Bond application for contracts ≤$500,000.
items.synopsis: SBA guarantees bid, performance, payment and ancillary bonds issued by participating sureties to small contractors who cannot get bonding alone. The contractor applies through an SBA-authorized surety agent. Quick Bond streamlines applications for contracts under $500K with no prior defaults and completion within 12 months.

eligibility.notes: Small under SBA size standards. As a 100% Black-owned firm it falls in the socially and economically disadvantaged class for the 90% tier under 13 CFR 115.31; the August 2026 8(a) rule amended 13 CFR 124.103 only, not Part 115.

items.fit: The most direct federal tool for the bonding-capacity goal and a prerequisite for most federal construction primes over $150K (Miller Act). Pairs with the MSBDFA program.
items.compliance_flag: ⚠ Confirm with the surety agent how SBA currently documents the 90% 'socially and economically disadvantaged' tier (self-certification vs. formal certification) given post-Ultima and EO 14173 practice.
items.verify_notes: Regulation: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-13/chapter-I/part-115. Exact contractor fee is set by Federal Register notice; Preferred Surety guarantee % not captured [VERIFY].

items.name: SBA Mentor-Protégé Program and joint ventures
items.award_amount: Non-monetary; mentor may provide bonding support, equity, loans and technical help; approved JV competes for small-business set-asides as a small business
items.synopsis: Pairs a small protégé with an experienced mentor; the approved agreement lets the pair form a JV that competes for small-business set-asides without affiliation. Protégé must be small, for-profit, and have a proposed mentor before applying via certify.sba.gov. Benefits explicitly include financial assistance such as bonding. SBA no longer approves JV agreements for competitive 8(a) awards.

eligibility.notes: Needs a willing mentor.

items.fit: Directly serves the 'partner with larger primes' and bonding goals; pairs with USACE/NAVFAC set-asides as a JV.
items.verify_notes: Portal: https://certify.sba.gov/mentor-protege-program.

items.name: SBA 7(a) Loan Program
items.funder: U.S. Small Business Administration (via participating lenders)
items.award_amount: Up to $5,000,000; standard guarantee % not stated on page [VERIFY]
items.synopsis: SBA's primary guaranteed loan program, delivered by banks. Covers equipment, working capital (including a monitored line-of-credit pilot) and real estate. Borrower must be for-profit, small, creditworthy and unable to get comparable credit elsewhere.

eligibility.notes: For-profit, small, U.S.-based.

items.fit: Direct match for equipment purchase and for working capital between pay applications on larger contracts.
items.verify_notes: Harbor Bank of Maryland (CDFI bank) and Delaware's True Access Capital are SBA lenders in the region.

items.name: SBA 504 Loan Program
items.funder: U.S. Small Business Administration via Certified Development Companies
items.award_amount: SBA portion up to $5M–$5.5M (page is inconsistent) [VERIFY]; long-term fixed rate
items.synopsis: Long-term fixed-rate financing for major fixed assets — machinery with 10+ year useful life, buildings, land — co-financed by a CDC and a senior lender. Not for working capital.

eligibility.notes: For-profit, small; must meet CDC credit standards.

items.fit: Good for heavy equipment (excavators, concrete equipment) or a yard/shop building.

items.name: SBA Microloan Program
items.funder: U.S. Small Business Administration via nonprofit intermediaries
items.award_amount: Up to $50,000 (average ~$13,000); up to 6-year terms; rates generally 8–13%
items.synopsis: Small loans through community intermediaries for equipment, supplies and working capital; cannot be used for real estate or to pay existing debt.
items.fit: Modest; useful for a tool or equipment purchase if bank financing is slow.

items.name: SBA 8(a) Business Development Program
items.award_amount: Access to 8(a) set-aside and sole-source contracts (sole-source ceiling $4.5M non-manufacturing); 9-year program. Personal thresholds: net worth ≤$850,000; AGI ≤$400,000; total assets ≤$6.5M.
items.synopsis: Nine-year program giving access to 8(a)-only competitions and sole-source awards. Requires 51% ownership by socially and economically disadvantaged citizens and two years in business. Final rule 91 FR 51568 (published 8/11/2026, effective 9/10/2026) eliminated the race-based presumption of social disadvantage: applicants must now document discrimination against an identifiable group they belong to plus resulting material harm to their own economic opportunity. Law-firm summaries of January 2026 SBA guidance report SBA no longer accepts post-Ultima narratives and approval volumes are very low.

eligibility.notes: Founded 2020 (meets 2-year rule) and small. Under the new 13 CFR 124.103, Black ownership alone does not satisfy social disadvantage; the owner would need documentary evidence of group-based discrimination and personal material harm, plus the economic thresholds.

items.fit: Historically the premier vehicle for a minority-owned GC to win larger federal construction; the path is now uncertain.
items.compliance_flag: ⚠ Legal review strongly recommended before applying — the new evidentiary standard is untested and self-certification carries false-statement exposure.
items.verify_notes: Rule: https://www.federalregister.gov/d/2026-16370. [VERIFY] January 2026 SBA guidance directly from SBA (secondary sources only were fetched).

items.name: SBA HUBZone Program
items.award_amount: HUBZone set-asides plus 10% price evaluation preference in full-and-open competitions
items.synopsis: Requires principal office in a HUBZone and at least 35% of employees residing in HUBZones. SBA states that during 2026 the map drops expiring Redesignated Areas; Qualified Census Tracts and Qualified Non-Metropolitan Counties refresh in July 2028.

eligibility.notes: The HUBZone map is script-rendered; no official page confirms or denies that Easton 21601 or Talbot County is a HUBZone.

items.fit: For a 1–10 person firm the 35% residency test is one or two people. Combined with the SBG 90% tier it would materially boost set-aside access.
items.verify_notes: Map: https://maps.certify.sba.gov/hubzone/map — see manual_checks.

items.name: Small Disadvantaged Business (SDB) self-certification in SAM.gov
items.award_amount: Not stated — counts toward large primes' SDB subcontracting goals under FAR 19.7
items.synopsis: Self-certification in SAM.gov Reps & Certs that lets federal primes count Cardinal toward SDB subcontracting goals.

eligibility.notes: SBA's SDB page could not be fetched; the August 2026 8(a) rule and EO 14173 may affect how SDB self-certification is treated.

items.fit: Relevant for subcontracting with USACE and NAVFAC primes.
items.compliance_flag: ⚠ Confirm current treatment of SDB self-certification after the 8(a) rule change.
